title: A Brazilian court fined lawyers for hidden instructions aimed at its AI
friendlyTitle: A Brazilian court fined lawyers for hiding instructions for its AI
summary: The 3rd Labor Court of Parauapebas fined two law firms after Galileu, the AI used by Brazil's National Justice Council, flagged white text on a white background in a filing. The hidden line told any AI reading the petition to review it superficially and not challenge the documents. The fine was 10 percent of the claim, about $16,000 on a claim of R$842,000. JetStream's English account is from 1 July. Brazilian outlet G1 reported the case on 14 May. It is on Hacker News now, with more than 260 points.
friendlySummary: A labor court in Parauapebas, Brazil, fined two law firms after the court's AI, called Galileu, found white writing on a white background in a legal filing. The hidden line told any AI reading the filing to look at it lightly and not question the documents. The fine was 10 percent of the claim, about $16,000 on a claim of R$842,000. The English write-up is from 1 July. A Brazilian news site reported the case on 14 May. People are reading it widely now.
whyItMatters: This is not a new ruling from this weekend. It is a settled example of what a court did when a filing tried to steer the reader that was a model. If you send a document an AI will read — a court, a client, a support desk — text a person cannot see is still text. If you receive one, look for text that does not show on the page.
